summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis was admitted for recurrent abdominal pain, generalized body aches, and poor oral intake, three days after a blood transfusion for iron deficiency anemia and black stools. Imaging showed no acute abdominal or intracranial findings, with stable cirrhosis and mild splenomegaly. Her pain was attributed to constipation, and she was treated with an aggressive bowel regimen including polyethylene glycol (Miralax) three times daily. Home pain medications were adjusted, reducing tramadol and discontinuing oxycodone to avoid worsening constipation. Her symptoms improved, she tolerated oral intake, and abdominal tenderness resolved. She was discharged home with instructions to continue the bowel regimen, restart iron supplements when tolerated, and follow up with her primary care and liver specialists. The urine culture showed contamination, and no active infection was treated.
